item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Wed Sep 30 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Wed Sep 30 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Wed Sep 30 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Cream & Crimson Scrimmage — Fri Oct 2, 6:00 PM — Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall
item.description: The Indiana men's basketball program will host an intrasquad scrimmage at 6 p.m. ET on Friday, Oct. 2, at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall. The event is open to the public, and doors will open at 4:30 p.m. ET. The Cream & Crimson Scrimmage will provide a firsthand look at the 2026-27 Indiana Hoosiers with player introductions, four quarters of scrimmaging, and an autograph session with the team. This event will be free to the public, and all parking lots will be open. Attendees will continue to operate under the Clear Bag Policy. Indiana brought in a seven-player transfer portal class, highlighted by Markus Burton (Notre Dame), Darren Harris (Duke), Bryce Lindsay (Villanova), Justin Monden (Maryland Eastern Shore), Jaeden Mustaf (Georgia Tech), Aiden Sherrell (Alabama), and Samet Yigitoglu (SMU). item.title: Harp Ensemble – Elżbieta Szmyt, director — Fri Oct 2, 7:00 PM — St. Paul Lutheran Church (Columbus
item.description: About the DirectorElżbieta Szmyt is professor of music, chair of the Harp Department, and director of the Harp Ensemble at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music. A native of Poland, she has made appearances on Polish radio and television, and performed numerous solo and chamber recitals in Europe, Canada, Japan, and the United States. She has been a featured soloist with the National Philharmonic Orchestra in Warsaw, the Cracow Philharmonic, Czech Radio Orchestra and the Metropolitan Orchestra of St. Louis. She has performed and given lectures for World Harp Congresses in Copenhagen, Prague, and Dublin. Her solo CD, Rhapsody, was released on the DUX label. Szmyt began her musical training at the age of 11 on piano and then began to study harp with Alina Baranowska while attending the J. Elsner School of Music in Warsaw. She continued studying harp at the Frederic Chopin Academy of Music in Warsaw. In 1987, she simultaneously earned two masters degrees, one from the Chopin Acade

item.title: Saturday Crafternoon at the Wylie House Museum — Sat Oct 3, 11:00 AM — 307 E 2nd St
item.description:
Fall at the Wylie House Museum with Bats, Brooms, andGourds! Get into the festive fall mood with mini brooms, corn husk bats, andgourds of all kinds. While the Wylie families were likely harvesting theircrops and preparing for a long winter, fall in modern times often means pumpkinsand gourds, scary stories and creepy creatures, and costumes and candy. Learnabout the folklore of brooms and bats and the check out the different types ofgourds grown on the property, and take home a packet of seeds to grow nextyear! Note: The Wylie House Museum will be closedOctober 9th and 10th for IU fall break. SaturdayCrafternoons are a free event for families, students, and friends of all ages!Activities change monthly. item.title: Writing in the Galleries — Sat Oct 3, 1:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description: In this program, we'll take a slow walk through the exhibition to discover what's here. Then you'll be prompted to select an artwork that speaks to you and express your thoughts and feelings on paper. Writing prompts will be provided. Read an overview of the exhibition Samuel Levi Jones: An Archeology of Knowledge (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/exhibitions/2026-09-12-samuel-levi-jones-archaeology-of-knowledge.html) What to Bringyour favorite pencil (no pens). a notebook or paper. Clipboards are available to borrow from the welcome desk on the first floor. a phone or camera to take a picture of the art for later reference, if you'd like to continue to write elsewhere. Know Before You GoArrive early, check in, and get ready for an on-time start.Readwhere to find us, where to park, accessibility, and museum guidelines.About Your Facilitator Dedaimia Whitney earned an MFA in fiction from Indiana University under the direction of Scott Russell Sanders. item.description: The Writers Guild at Bloomington partners with the Lotus Education & Arts Foundation to present a poetry reading at the 33rd annual Lotus World Music & Arts Festival, featuring Tony Brewer, Hiromi Yoshida, and Dylan Kennedy. Writers Guild Mission The Writers Guild at Bloomington is an association of writers committed to mutual support and the professional development of their craft. We foster interaction among writers as well as other artists, educators, and the Monroe County public, thereby enhancing the vibrancy of the arts and the writing community in the greater Bloomington area. Featured Artists & Bios Tony Brewer is a poet and audio artist from Bloomington, Indiana. He has published 13 books and chapbooks, most recently Chin Music (OAC Press, 2026). Tony has been offering Poetry On Demand at coffeehouses, museums, cemeteries, churches, bars, and art and music festivals for over fifteen years and was named Indiana’s 2024 Literary Champion by Indiana Humanities. item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Oct 5 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Oct 5 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery.
